design.decision: Lead low [♦]s while opponents still hold [♦] (each one now wins), follow a [♦] lead with your lowest [♦] instead of the honor, and bid [♦] length as tricks.
design.opponent: Revealed the first time a low [♦] takes an opponent's honor. From then on opponents can only win [♦] tricks by voiding and trumping, so they discard [♦]s early.
design.rationale: This is a card-strength rule on a narrow card set, the family the brief says measures well. I would buy it before knowing my build, because any [♦]s become sure winners in [♦] tricks. The brief's lesson about low ranks applies to [♠], where low cards become top trumps. A side suit never beats trumps, so the counterplay of voiding and trumping stays intact. Combined with the kept untrumpable [♦] it makes the [♦] length line a real plan. My estimate puts it close to uc-twos-beat (+14.6). A rule has no amount to retune, so it may need to move to rare.
